hello.note: Also used for goodbye. Casual: היי (hai).

please.note: Also used for 'here you go' and as a reply to thanks.

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: תודה רבה (toda raba).

sorry.note: A woman says: מצטערת (mitsta'eret). For small slips, סליחה (slicha) is enough.

how_are_you.note: To a woman: ma shlomech (same spelling). Casual: מה נשמע? (ma nishma?)

whats_your_name.note: To a woman: eich kor'im lach? (same spelling).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Common reply: גם לי (gam li), 'me too'.

where_from.note: To a woman: מאיפה את? (me'eifo at?)

im_from.note: מ (mi-; me- before א, ה, ע, ר) is joined to the country: אני מקנדה (ani mikanada), מאנגליה (me'anglia).

speak_english.note: To a woman: את מדברת אנגלית? (at medaberet anglit?)

dont_understand.note: A woman says: אני לא מבינה (ani lo mevina).

speak_slowly.note: אפשר (efshar) + verb is a polite request that works for anyone, man or woman.

where_bathroom.note: Start with סליחה (slicha) to be polite.

can_you_help.note: To a woman: את יכולה לעזור לי? (at yechola la'azor li?)

one.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: אחד (echad).

two.note: Counting form. Masculine: שניים (shnayim). Right before a noun: שתי / שני (shtei / shnei).

three.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: שלושה (shlosha).

four.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: ארבעה (arba'a).

five.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: חמישה (chamisha).

six.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: שישה (shisha).

seven.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: שבעה (shiv'a).

eight.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: shmona (same spelling).

nine.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: תשעה (tish'a).

ten.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: עשרה (asara).

water.note: A glass of water: כוס מים (kos mayim).

coffee.note: The Israeli milky coffee (like a latte) is הפוך (hafuch).

im_hungry.note: A woman says: אני רעבה (ani re'eva).

no_meat.note: A woman says: אני לא אוכלת בשר (ani lo ochelet basar).

stop_here.note: To a woman driver: תעצרי פה, בבקשה (ta'atsri po, bevakasha).

airport.note: Ben Gurion Airport is usually just called נתב״ג (natbag).

want_to_go.note: A woman says ani rotsa (same spelling). ל (le-) is joined to the place: לחיפה (lecheifa).

one_ticket.note: Most buses and trains take the רב-קו (rav-kav) smart card instead.

id_like_this.note: A woman says ani rotsa (same spelling). Also: אני אקח את זה (ani ekach et ze), 'I'll take it'.

just_looking.note: A woman says: אני רק מסתכלת, תודה (ani rak mistakelet, toda).

pay_card.note: אשראי (ashrai), literally 'credit', is everyday shorthand for a credit card. בכרטיס (bekartis), 'by card', also works.

see_you_later.note: Also: נתראה אחר כך (nitra'e achar kach).

wait_moment.note: Or: חכה רגע (chake rega); to a woman: חכי רגע (chaki rega).

call_police.note: Plural, shouted to everyone around. Police emergency number in Israel: 100.

need_doctor.note: A woman says: אני צריכה רופא (ani tsricha rofe). Ambulance (Magen David Adom): 101.

dont_feel_well.note: A woman says: אני לא מרגישה טוב (ani lo margisha tov).

lost_phone.note: A mobile phone is also commonly called פלאפון (pelefon).

allergic.note: A woman says: אני אלרגית ל… (ani alergit le…).

be_careful.note: To a woman: תיזהרי! (tizahari!). Also: זהירות! (zehirut!)

dont_know.note: A woman says: אני לא יודעת (ani lo yoda'at).

i_like_it.note: A woman says ani ohevet (אוהבת). Also: זה מוצא חן בעיניי (ze motse chen be'einai).

dont_like_it.note: A woman says: אני לא אוהבת את זה (ani lo ohevet et ze).

im_tired.note: A woman says: אני עייפה (ani ayefa).

im_happy.note: A woman says: אני שמחה (ani smecha).

welcome.note: To a woman: ברוכה הבאה (brucha haba'a); to a group: ברוכים הבאים (bruchim haba'im).

congratulations.note: For an achievement, Israelis often say כל הכבוד (kol hakavod).

mother.note: Formal or written: אם (em). My mother: אמא שלי (ima sheli).

father.note: Formal or written: אב (av). My father: אבא שלי (aba sheli).

brother.note: My brother: האח שלי (ha'ach sheli) or אחי (achi), which is also slang for 'bro'.

sister.note: My sister: אחותי (achoti) or האחות שלי (ha'achot sheli). Also means 'nurse'.

child.note: Of a daughter: ילדה (yalda). To be specific: son בן (ben), daughter בת (bat).

friend.note: A female friend: חברה (chavera). Both can also mean boyfriend / girlfriend.

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: זאת חברה שלי (zot chavera sheli). החבר שלי (hachaver sheli) can mean 'my boyfriend'.

are_you_married.note: To a woman: את נשואה? (at nesu'a?)

have_children.note: To a woman: yesh lach yeladim? (same spelling).

monday.note: Literally 'the second day': the Israeli week starts on Sunday. Weekdays are often said without יום: שני (sheni).

friday.note: Friday evening, when Shabbat begins: ערב שבת (erev shabat).

saturday.note: Also: יום שבת (yom shabat). The day of rest: many shops close and most public transport stops.

sunday.note: In Israel this is the first working day of the week.

weekend.note: Often shortened to סופ״ש (sofash). In Israel it means Friday and Saturday.

next_week.note: As a noun: השבוע הבא (hashavua haba).

eleven.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: אחד עשר (achad asar).

twelve.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: שנים עשר (shneim asar).

fifteen.note: Counting form. With masculine nouns: חמישה עשר (chamisha asar).

twenty.note: The tens are the same with masculine and feminine nouns.

how_old.note: To a woman: בת כמה את? (bat kama at?)

years_old.note: A woman says: אני בת … (ani bat …). Literally 'I'm a son of …'.

this_one.note: For a feminine noun: הזאת (hazot). When asking for it: את הזה (et haze).

another_one.note: For a feminine noun: עוד אחת (od achat).

its_sunny.note: Also: שמשי היום (shimshi hayom), using the adjective 'sunny'.

have_reservation.note: Also: הזמנתי חדר (hizmanti cheder), 'I booked a room'.

luggage.note: One suitcase: מזוודה (mizvada). On airport signs: כבודה (kvuda).

check_out_time.text: עד מתי צריך לפנות את החדר?
check_out_time.roman: ad matai tsarich lefanot et hacheder?
check_out_time.note: Literally 'until when must one vacate the room?'. The English word צ'ק-אאוט (check-out) is also used.

what_do_you_do.note: To a woman: במה את עובדת? (bema at ovedet?). Also: מה אתה עושה בחיים? (ma ata ose bachayim?)

i_work_in.note: A woman says: אני עובדת ב… (ani ovedet be…). ב joins the next word: בבנק (babank), 'at the bank'.

im_student.note: A woman says: אני סטודנטית (ani studentit). A school pupil is תלמיד (talmid).

meeting.note: A team or staff meeting is often ישיבה (yeshiva).

im_busy.note: A woman says: אני עסוקה (ani asuka).

colleague.note: A woman: עמיתה לעבודה (amita la'avoda). Casual: חבר לעבודה (chaver la'avoda).

lets_start.note: To a group. To one man: בוא נתחיל (bo natchil); to a woman: בואי נתחיל (bo'i natchil).

good_job.note: Also: עבודה טובה! (avoda tova!) or יפה מאוד! (yafe me'od!)

what_recommend.note: To a woman: מה את ממליצה? (ma at mamlitsa?). For anyone: מה מומלץ פה? (ma mumlats po?)

not_spicy.note: Literally 'without the hot stuff'. Also: לא חריף, בבקשה (lo charif, bevakasha).

vegetarian_food.note: I'm vegetarian: אני צמחוני (ani tsimchoni); a woman: צמחונית (tsimchonit). Vegan: טבעוני (tiv'oni).

more_water.note: Also: אפשר עוד מים? (efshar od mayim?)

im_full.note: A woman says: אני שבעה (ani sve'a). Casual: אני מפוצץ (ani mefotsats), 'I'm stuffed'.

takeaway.note: You may be asked: לשבת או לקחת? (lashevet o lakachat?), 'eat in or take away?'

it_was_delicious.note: Also: היה מעולה (haya me'ule), 'it was excellent'.

keep_change.note: To a woman: תשאירי את העודף (tash'iri et ha'odef).

stomach.note: The everyday word, as in 'stomach ache'. The organ itself is קיבה (keiva).

call_ambulance.note: Plural, shouted to everyone around. To one man: תזמין אמבולנס (tazmin ambulans). Ambulance number: 101.

need_rest.note: A woman says: אני צריכה לנוח (ani tsricha lanuach).

feel_better.note: A woman says: אני מרגישה יותר טוב (ani margisha yoter tov).

get_well.note: Also: תרגיש טוב! (targish tov!); to a woman: תרגישי טוב! (targishi tov!)

lets_meet.note: To a woman: בואי ניפגש (bo'i nipagesh); to a group: בואו ניפגש (bo'u nipagesh).

are_you_free.note: To a woman: את פנויה מחר? (at pnuya machar?). Also: יש לך זמן מחר? (yesh lecha zman machar?)

call_me.note: To a woman: תתקשרי אליי (titkashri elai).

your_number.note: To a woman: ma mispar hatelefon shelach? (same spelling). Short: מה המספר שלך? (ma hamispar shelcha?)

have_nice_day.note: To a woman: sheyihye lach yom tov (same spelling). Short: יום טוב! (yom tov!)

happy_birthday.note: Israelis also say מזל טוב! (mazal tov!) on birthdays.

miss_you.note: A woman says מתגעגעת (mitga'aga'at). To a woman: אלייך (elayich).
